To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we propose an approach for learning from restricted action spaces, (b) we demonstrate that this approach accelerates learning in complex StarCraft tasks, (c) we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in a variety of control tasks, and (d) we demonstrate that our approach is effective in large-scale, multi-agent StarCraft tasks with large, combinatorial action-spaces
we can learn to play a game with a very large number of possible actions (up to 10000) by starting with a smaller game and gradually increasing its action space.
we can learn to solve StarCraft micro-management tasks using reinforcement learning by restricting the action space and growing it over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to efficiently explore and learn in complex environments.
how to learn efficiently in complex, large action spaces, where traditional random exploration is too inefficient to be effective.
the problem of how to learn from a limited number of samples in complex environments, and how to transfer the learned knowledge from restricted action spaces into full action spaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have shown that a curriculum of progressively increasing action spaces can accelerate reinforcement learning.
we have developed a method for learning to solve complex tasks by growing action spaces and demonstrated its effectiveness in challenging micromanagement tasks in the StarCraft environment.
our approach of growing action spaces is a promising direction for improving the sample efficiency of reinforcement learning in complex environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can use a curriculum of growing action spaces to learn in a more efficient and effective manner, and we can do this without any changes to the underlying reinforcement learning algorithms.
we can train agents to solve complex tasks with large combinatoral action spaces using a curriculum of progressively expanding action spaces.
we propose to use off-policy RL to estimate optimal value function for multiple action spaces at the same time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to use off-policy reinforcement learning for efficient transfer learning between tasks with different action spaces.
, when learning is difficult, we can use a curriculum of restricted action spaces to accelerate the agent’s progress and achieve faster learning.
, in some settings, the agent can learn to perform well in a task with large, complex action spaces by first learning in a task with smaller action spaces.
